nodes.label: Email Verification Security Notice
nodes.rationale: For security, saving profile/credential changes first requires email verification: a 6-digit code is sent to the user's registered Gmail address and must be confirmed (via the verificar_codigo page) before the changes are applied, preventing unauthorized account takeover if a session is compromised.

nodes.label: Constrained Query Vocabulary Expansion
nodes.rationale: graphify query's substring+IDF matcher has no stemming, synonyms, or cross-language matching, so a wording mismatch between the user's question and the graph's node-label vocabulary would silently collapse the answer to noise. Expanding the query against the extracted vocabulary (without inventing tokens) before traversal fixes this.

nodes.label: Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge (use AMBIGUOUS if unsure); never skip the corpus-size check warning; always show token cost in the report; never hide cohesion scores behind symbols; never run HTML viz on a graph with more than 5,000 nodes without warning the user. These rules keep the extraction pipeline auditable and trustworthy.

nodes.label: Confidence Score Rubric
nodes.rationale: Discrete confidence buckets (1.0 EXTRACTED; 0.95/0.85/0.75/0.65/0.55 for INFERRED; 0.1-0.3 AMBIGUOUS) replace a continuous 0-1 range because production data showed models collapse continuous guidance into a bimodal distribution (>50% at 0.5, >40% at 0.85+); discrete rubrics are followed more reliably than ranges.

nodes.label: Node ID Format Rule
nodes.rationale: Node IDs must use the full repo-relative path (every directory segment) joined with underscores plus the normalized entity name, matching the AST extractor's ID scheme exactly. Using only the filename or the immediate parent directory creates orphan ghost-duplicate nodes when two files share a name in different directories.

nodes.label: Graph Shrink Guard (#479)
nodes.rationale: to_json() refuses to write graph.json when the newly built graph has fewer nodes than the existing one (#479), preventing a bad or partial extraction from silently clobbering a good graph. GRAPH_REPORT.md and the analysis sidecar are written only after a successful (non-shrinking) export, so they never describe a graph that graph.json doesn't actually contain.
